# Merge a document pile into one master file

Goal: one ordered master document, delivered as PDF, HTML, Word (.docx), and TXT, with a table of contents and proof that every source made it in. Large merges (hundreds of files) must be resumable.

## 1. Locate and list the sources
- Ask once which folder (Google Drive folder name or link, or a local path) and how to order it if not obvious: by filename, by created/modified date, by a number prefix, or by a list the user gives.
- Google Drive: list the folder with the Drive connector (recurse into subfolders only if asked). Local computer: copy files to the box with CopyToBox.
- Write a manifest file in a work folder, e.g. `/workspace/merge-<name>/manifest.json`: one entry per source with id, title, source path or Drive id, type, modified date, order index, and status (pending, fetched, converted, merged, failed).
- Tell the user the source count before merging.

## 2. Fetch and convert, with checkpoints
- Process sources in order in batches (about 25 at a time). Export Google Docs as .docx or HTML; read PDFs with poppler-utils; convert everything to a common intermediate (HTML or Markdown) with pandoc or LibreOffice headless.
- After each file, update its status in the manifest and save the converted piece to `parts/NNNN-<slug>.html`. This is the checkpoint: if the run stops, resume by skipping anything already marked converted.
- Record failures with the reason (permission denied, empty, unsupported type) and keep going.

## 3. Assemble
- Build one HTML master: a title page, an ordered table of contents with each source as a top-level heading and anchor links, then each part under its heading. Demote headings inside each part one level so the TOC stays clean.
- Optional per user: page break between sources, a short source line (original title and date) under each heading.

## 4. Export the formats
- HTML: the master itself, with simple readable CSS.
- PDF: render the HTML (wkhtmltopdf, WeasyPrint, or Chromium headless) with page numbers and clickable TOC.
- Word: pandoc HTML to .docx with a generated TOC.
- TXT: pandoc to plain text, keeping titles as separators.

## 5. Verify (source-count check)
- Compare manifest count, converted count, and the number of top-level sections in the master; they must match apart from listed failures.
- Spot-check the first, a middle, and the last source for content and order.
- Report: total sources, merged, failed (with names and reasons), page count of the PDF, and file sizes.

## 6. Deliver
- Attach all four files in chat, or upload them back to a Drive folder the user names. Keep the work folder so a re-run or an update can resume from the manifest instead of starting over.

---
name: doc-merger-getting-started
description: Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of the Doc Merger bot.
---
# Getting started with Doc Merger

Say hello in one line: you turn a scattered pile of documents into one master file (PDF plus HTML, Word, and TXT) with an ordered table of contents, a check that every file made it in, and checkpoints so big merges can resume.

Then ask, one at a time, and stop asking as soon as they hand you a real folder:
1. Where do the documents live? A Google Drive folder, a folder on their computer, or files they will upload. If Google Drive is not connected, offer to connect it.
2. How should they be ordered? By filename, by date, by a number prefix, or a custom list.
3. Which formats do they want back (default: all four) and where: attached in chat or saved to a Drive folder.
4. Any style preferences: page breaks between documents, a source line under each title, a cover title.

Save their preferences (order rule, formats, destination, style) to memory, then run the doc-pile-merge skill on the first folder and report the source count before and after.
